newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weak as spot market suffers.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weak as spot market suffers.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended weak after a shortened session on Monday, under pressure from sloppy physical market fundamentals in Northwest Europe, dealers said.

April Brent closed 13 cents lower at $20.36 a barrel, at the bottom of an 18-cent range posted in extremely light volume as many traders left their desks for industry functions on the first day of Institute of Petroleum Week.
Interest was also subdued during the afternoon by the absence of U.S. dealing thanks to the President's Day holiday.
"It was very difficult to get anything done today but the tone is still soft," said a broker.

Traders said spot North Sea crude markets were amply supplied despite the suspension of loadings at Norway's Statfjord and Gullfaks fields due to high winds. Production at both fields was normal, operator Statoil said.
Berthing at the Sullom Voe Brent terminal on the Shetland Islands was also suspended because of the weather.
Traders said refinery demand was slow.
Meanwhile, March gas oil also ended weaker, slipping 75 cents to $177.50 a tonne.
